summary: Iter11 targeted regression on login lockout bug fix. Wrote /app/backend/tests/backend_test_iter11_lockout.py with 6 focused tests, all PASS. Verified: (1) first wrong pw = 401, (2) 5 wrong = 401 each + 6th = 429 with body containing 'Too many failed attempts' AND a specific '<N> minute(s)' phrase (NOT 'a few minutes'); observed message uses 15-minute countdown, (3) during lockout even correct admin pw returns 429 (lockout wins), (4) forgot-password returns {ok:true,message:...}, deletes login_attempts entry for 'login:<email>', and rotates password_hash so pre-existing correct pw now 401s, (5) cooldown-expiry code path (server.py 751-764) works: seeded a past locked_until, next failed attempt cleared the entry and restarted count at 1 with locked_until=None — exactly as the fix specifies, (6) admin login end-to-end with seeded creds returns access_token + must_reset_password=true. Admin password restored to ADMIN_TEMP_PASSWORD after forgot-password test.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py L751-764: cooldown-expiry branch correctly (a) parses locked_until into an aware datetime, (b) if still in future returns 429 with mins = ceil-ish((lu-now)/60)+1 → always >=1 (message formatting handles singular/plural), (c) if expired, DELETES the login_attempts entry and sets lock=None so the very next code block treats prev_count as 0. Bug is fully fixed.

server.py L769-779: on failed auth, prev_count comes from `lock.get('count',0) if lock else 0` — because we just nulled lock on cooldown-expiry, a stale 5-count is guaranteed to reset to new_count=1. Verified by test_cooldown_expiry_resets_counter reading Mongo directly.

server.py L881-882: forgot-password explicitly deletes {'_id':'login:<email>'} which clears the failed-login lockout independent of its own throttle bucket ('forgot:<email>'). Good separation of buckets — the forgot throttle cannot lock out the login path and vice-versa.

server.py L832-889: forgot-password always returns the generic {ok:true,message} regardless of user existence — no user enumeration. Only downside: throttle bucket uses same login_attempts collection with a different '_id' prefix; sharing the collection is fine but a comment noting the two disjoint key namespaces would help future maintainers.

Minor: at L756 the formula `int((lu-now_ts).total_seconds()//60)+1` will report '16 minutes' immediately after the lock is set (because 15*60s // 60 = 15, +1 = 16). That's off-by-one on the friendly side (says 16 when actual max is 15). Not a bug per se but message could say 'up to 15 minutes' or use ceil without the +1. Consider capping with min(15, mins) to match the actual 15-min TTL. Non-blocking; user-facing wording is still specific and correct-ish.

rca_of_the_issue: Original bug: login_attempts counter only ever incremented; the 15-min lockout window expired but the row (count>=5, locked_until in past) stayed in Mongo. Every subsequent failed login re-computed new_count = old_count+1 >= 5, so `locked_until` got rewritten to now+15min on EVERY failure forever. The fix (L762-764) deletes the row when the previous lockout window has expired and treats it as fresh (lock=None), so the next failed attempt starts new_count at 1 and only re-locks after 5 fresh failures. Verified end-to-end by test_cooldown_expiry_resets_counter.
